newsitem.title: USA: Young man to be charged in murder of Cosby's son.
newsitem.headline: Young man to be charged in murder of Cosby's son.

text.p: Los Angeles authorities on Thursday were preparing charges against a young white male for the roadside murder of entertainer Bill Cosby's only son, Ennis.

Police were also questioning two others in the Jan. 16 killing, which captured national attention but lacked a solid breakthrough before the suspect's arrest on Wednesday night. A spokeswoman for the Los Angeles County District Attorney's office said prosecutors from the major crimes division were reviewing the case and any charges would likely be filed on Friday.
"We're reviewing the case today. If there is a filing, it's likely to be tomorrow," spokeswoman Suzanne Childs said.

Cosby, who lives in New York with his wife Camille and was told of the arrest at midnight, said in a statement on Thursday, "We want to thank the L.A.P.D. (Los Angeles Police Department). We realise how tough it must have been on them every day. We always had every hope that they would find the suspect and that jurisprudence would proceed."

Gavin de Becker, an adviser to the Cosby family who worked closely with police during the investigation, said in a statement on Thursday the "caution and care" taken by the police "will make the journey from arrest to conviction a successful one."

Los Angeles Police Chief Willie Williams told a late-night news conference on Wednesday the unidentified man "will be charged with the murder of Ennis Cosby." The decision on whether to charge a suspect in a felony case such as murder normally rests with the district attorney and Williams indicated police had been working closely with prosecutors.

"We are very comfortable, based on our work with the district attorney and other evidence that has been gathered, that this is the man and he is the shooter," Williams said. He said the suspect closely resembled a composite sketch that was issued shortly after Ennis Cosby was murdered.

A report in Thursday's Los Angeles Times quoted unnamed sources as saying police believed a gang of "Russian" robbers may have taken part in the murder and that somebody "came forward" and gave information to the police to settle a score with the suspect and his possible accomplices.
A police spokesman refused to comment on the report.

Williams said the suspect was put under surveillance by the L.A.P.D.'s special investigations unit on Wednesday morning and arrested that night. He said the suspect lived in the San Fernando Valley area of Los Angeles.
Police continued to question two other people, a man and a woman, in connection with the murder, but Williams said they were not under arrest.

David Brokaw, the Cosby family's spokesman, said he had talked to Cosby and his wife following the suspect's arrest. "I sensed a real sense of triumph and exuberance and something along the lines of some sort of closure," Brokaw said on the NBC "Today" programme.
He said Camille Cosby was particularly happy with the arrest. "She said ... 'I want this man, and I want him convicted, and I want him sentenced, and I want him to go to jail.'"

James Anderson, director of public relations for the Cosby Show, said: "For the immediate future Mr. Cosby and his family will not be making any more statements or giving any other interviews. Mr. Cosby and his family hope the public will allow them the chance to have as much privacy as possible during this period."

Ennis Cosby, 27, was shot to death in the early morning while changing a flat tire near a freeway off-ramp in an exclusive suburb of Los Angeles. Cosby described his son as "my hero" after his murder, referring to his overcoming a severe learning disability to succeed in college and go on to a doctoral programme at Columbia University in New York.
